chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, from some of his teachers, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about al-Qa'im (peace be upon him), and he said: "The diviners (of the time) tell lies. We, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not fix a specific time." Then he said: "Allah does not consent save to reverse the timing of the diviners."

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتٍ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Awakened One / The Awaited Imam
key_terms.الْوَقَاتُونَ: Those who fix/assign specific times (for the reappearance)
key_terms.يُوَقِّتُونَ: To fix or designate a specific time

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about fixing a specific time for the appearance of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the common misconception that the Ahl al-Bayt fixed a specific date for the Mahdi's appearance, emphasizing that 'waqqatin' (those who assign times) are distinct from the Imams themselves. He concludes with a divine promise that Allah will nullify the specific times calculated by those who attempt to predict the unseen, reinforcing the concept of *Tawqif* (divine appointment) over human speculation. This distinction is crucial in Shia eschatology to preserve the authority of the Imams in determining the exact moment of reappearance.
